content:
maria: Heads up — after the 11:30 rollout the longctx worker pool on prod-3 started hitting OOMs with requests >= 8k seq. Canary repros the same.
kevin: Ugh. Any obvious log traces? which commit rolled?
maria: rolled PR f3b2a9e (kv: slab allocator tuning + swap threshold tweak). Logs show repeated `OutOfMemory` then `slab_swap_out failed` and kernel oom_killer activity.
maria: repro command I used:
```bash
# run locally against canary
curl -X POST https://canary-api/runs -d '{"model":"redwood-long","input_len":8192, "batch":1}'
```
jon: Can you paste the tail of the worker log around the OOM?
maria: snippet:
```
[2026-02-12T11:33:02Z] worker[42]: Alloc failed: 2147483648 bytes
[2026-02-12T11:33:02Z] worker[42]: slab: tried to swap_out but free_pages low
[2026-02-12T11:33:03Z] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 4231 (runtime) score 987 or sacrifice child
```
kevin: CI perf bot flagged a regression earlier today too — ci-bot: `perf/regression: p95 latency +7% for seq>=4096` (post-merge).
ci-bot: detected: PR f3b2a9e increased memory churn on long sequences; perf-run-2026-02-12 attached (summary).
jon: Hmm, allocator change could be shifting eviction order so large KV entries are being swapped more often, causing fragmentation and spike in allocation latency. That would also change kernel selection behavior for long sequences (we pick different kernels when mem pressure/fragmentation changes).
kevin: Good call. If kernel selection is toggling mid-request or choosing a slower fallback kernel, that could explain both latency and memory churn.
sre-oncall: Are we seeing this only on prod-3? Any region differences?
maria: Only prod-3 so far (same hw profile). Canary and prod-3 both repro. staging with older images is fine.
kevin: I'm running a quick bisect: reverting the slab threshold in f3b2a9e -> f3b2a9e~1 locally. If that fixes canary I'll push a rollback.
kevin: repro after local revert: no OOM within 30 runs, p95 back to baseline.
jon: Can we also capture a perf profile of allocator ops across runs? A flamegraph of `malloc`/`kv_alloc` would help.
maria: uploaded perf dump to S3: s3://rwd-perf/2026-02-12/longctx-slabs/{trace}. Link posted in thread.
ci-bot: perf summary:
```
seq>=4096: p95 latency 201ms -> 215ms (+6.9%)
alloc failures per-min: 0.03 -> 1.2
kv-evict ops/sec: 12 -> 68
```
kevin: Plan: revert f3b2a9e in prod-3 now (hotfix), add temporary kernel-selection guard to prefer stable kernels for seq>4096, and open follow-up to redesign slab thresholds + add more unit tests for fragmentation.
maria: rolling revert patch to prod-3 now.
kevin: Revert deployed to prod-3, monitoring.
sre-oncall: Marking as rollout-blocker for today. I'll standby for rollback verification.
maria: After revert, no OOM for 20m on the same workload, p95 back to expected.
jon: We'll need a root-cause: probably the swap threshold made the allocator prefer smaller slab sizes causing inter-slab fragmentation and increased evict churn. Also add a safety: if evict ops/sec spikes >50, fallback to prev allocator config.
kevin: Filing follow-up RFC: "slab-thresholds-and-kernel-routing-for-longctx" with repro/trace links.
maria: Thanks all. Adding postmortem tag and PR link in #postmortems after we finalize root cause. :thumbsup:
kevin: Nice quick triage everyone.
ci-bot: test-summary: nightly-regression-check queued to run full workload matrix.
jon: Assigning to @jon and @maria for root cause + fix PR.
maria: on it — I'll include an extended stress job in CI for seq len 4k-16k.
kevin: closing loop once staging-green and no regressions in 24h. :eyes:
